Order
05.01.2026 Order No.
05. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the Informant.

2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with C.T. Case No.801 of 2023 pending on the file of learned JMFC-III, Bhubaneswar, arising out of Sahid Nagar P.S. Case No.319 of 2023 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 420 and 34 of IPC.

3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner's husband was a Director of the company and after passing away of the husband, the Petitioner has been inducted as the Director, hence her complicity is limited and it is submitted that the principal accused Chitrasen Behera is in custody.
Hence, taking into account the limited role ascribed to the Petitioner and the nature of transaction, the Petitioner who is a lady may be protected by pre-arrest bail.
4. Learned counsel for the State as well as Informant oppose the prayer for pre-arrest bail.

5. Learned counsel for the Informant submits that the principal accused introduced the present Petitioner as one of the Directors and she has equal complicity in the matter, since her husband was at the helm of the affairs and it is submitted that the two cheques which were issued by the present Petitioner have not been honored which is also fortified by the submission of the learned counsel for the State.

sentences.text: 1 6. Referring to the same, it is further submitted that from the very inception the Petitioner had the mens-rea to commit the offence.
Hence, the bogey of civil liability and contractual obligation ought not to be taken into account.

7. On a conspectus of materials on record, nature of the allegations, the background in which the same is levelled and the role ascribed to the Petitioner, this Court is persuaded to hold that the Petitioner is entitled to be protected by pre-arrest bail.

Hence, it is directed that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioner shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper.
8. Additionally it is directed the Petitioner shall not leave the Country without the specific permission of the learned Court in seisin.
9. It is needless to state that the Petitioner shall cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
10. The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Ayesha Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Puspanjali Patra vs State Of Odisha ....
